record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: Is the equidistribution of saddle periodic points exponentially fast against Hölder observables, and is the analogous weighted convergence to μ_φ also exponentially fast?

evidence.quote: Question 36. — Is the convergence (6) exponentially fast against Hölder continuous observables? Is that also the case for (7)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ be a complex Hénon map, i.e., a finite composition of generalized Hénon maps of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(y,p(y)-ax)$ with $a\in\mathbb{C}^*$ and $p$ a one-variable polynomial of degree $\geq 2$. Let $d\geq 2$ denote its dynamical degree, let $\mu$ be its unique measure of maximal entropy, and for $n\geq 1$ let $P_n$ denote the set of saddle periodic points of period $n$. It is known that
$$\frac{1}{d^n}\sum_{p\in P_n}\delta_p\;\longrightarrow\;\mu \qquad (\ast)$$
weakly as $n\to\infty$, and more generally, for a continuous plurisubharmonic potential $\varphi$ with associated weighted equilibrium measure $\mu_\varphi$, an analogous weighted convergence
$$\frac{1}{d^n}\sum_{p\in P_n} e^{S_n\varphi(p)}\,\delta_p\;\longrightarrow\;\mu_\varphi \qquad (\ast\ast)$$
holds (where $S_n\varphi=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\varphi\circ f^k$, suitably normalized).

Question: Does the convergence in $(\ast)$ hold at an exponential rate against Hölder continuous test functions? That is, does there exist $\lambda\in(0,1)$ such that for every Hölder continuous observable $\psi$ on a fixed neighborhood of the support of $\mu$,
$$\left|\frac{1}{d^n}\sum_{p\in P_n}\psi(p)-\int\psi\,d\mu\right|=O(\lambda^n)\,\|\psi\|_{\mathrm{Höl}}?$$
Does the analogous exponential convergence hold for $(\ast\ast)$ with limit $\mu_\varphi$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2025) establishes equidistribution of saddle periodic points for Hénon-like maps in any dimension, and separate work shows the measure of maximal entropy of every complex Hénon map is exponentially mixing of all orders for Hölder observables. However, none of these results explicitly establish an exponential rate for the equidistribution of saddle periodic points themselves against Hölder observables, nor for the weighted convergence to μ_φ. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of saddle periodic points for Hénon-like maps
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 1.1 establishes that saddle periodic points equidistribute with respect to the equilibrium measure as n→∞, but focuses on the limiting behavior rather than convergence rates.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work establishes qualitative equidistribution but does not give an exponential rate against Hölder observables.

status_evidence.title: Every complex Hénon map is exponentially mixing of all orders and satisfies the CLT
status_evidence.snippet: The measure of maximal entropy of every complex Hénon map is exponentially mixing of all orders for Hölder observables.
status_evidence.claim: Exponential mixing for the measure μ is known, but this concerns mixing, not the rate of periodic-point equidistribution.

status_evidence.title: Hénon Maps: A List of Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems concerning Hénon maps, including questions about rates of equidistribution.
